intent.raw_query: Mexico City food and culture, $900 solo, 5 days, any month 2026

experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tacos, and artisanal products. Chat with local vendors and discover ingredients central to Mexican cuisine.

experiences.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids & Street Food
experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec pyramids of the Sun and Moon, one of the most iconic archaeological sites in the Americas. On the way back, stop at a local roadside stall for authentic barbacoa tacos and pulque, a traditional fermented agave drink.
experiences.location: Teotihuacan, State of Mexico (day trip from Mexico City)

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood Walk & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Stroll through the bohemian cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, visit the colorful Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul), and enjoy local street food like tostadas and churros from the central market. A deeply cultural and artistic experience.

experiences.name: Roma & Condesa Taco Crawl
experiences.description: Wander through the trendy, tree-lined neighborhoods of Roma and Condesa sampling tacos al pastor, quesadillas, and elotes from beloved street stalls and taquerías. This self-guided food crawl showcases the vibrant everyday food culture of chilangos (Mexico City locals).

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Walking Tour
experiences.description: Admire the stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture of the Palacio de Bellas Artes, view Diego Rivera's famous murals inside, and walk through the historic Zócalo plaza. Explore centuries of Mexican history, politics, and art all within a few walkable blocks.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle into Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — arrival is in the evening. Prepare for the trip ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City airport at 22:30. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal Aérea station (very budget-friendly at ~5 MXN) or a pre-booked authorized airport taxi to the hotel. Check in, freshen up, and take a short walk around the immediate neighborhood to get oriented.

meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a nearby taqueria or street food stall near the hotel. Look for tacos de canasta or tortas for under 50 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Only use official airport taxis or pre-booked ride services to avoid scams. Metro is the cheapest option at ~5 MXN per ride. Keep cash in small denominations handy for street food and transport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the historic Centro Histórico on foot. Explore the massive Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world — completely free. Walk to the Templo Mayor ruins and museum (entry ~80 MXN) to learn about Aztec history. Admire the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral exterior for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior and peek at murals inside (free entry to ground floor). Walk through Alameda Central park, a beautiful green space popular with locals. Visit the Mercado de Artesanías nearby to browse local crafts. Stroll down Avenida Madero, a pedestrian-only street full of street performers and free architectural wonders.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Barrio Chino (Chinatown) area near Centro for a unique cultural mix. Enjoy the vibrant street life and browse evening markets. Return to hotel via Metro.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local market breakfast stall near the hotel — try chilaquiles or tamales with atole for around 50–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan or Mercado Arcos de Belem near Centro — fresh comida corrida (set lunch menu) for 60–90 MXN including soup, main, and drink.
meals.dinner: Street tacos near Zócalo — tacos de barbacoa, al pastor, or suadero for 15–25 MXN each. Budget around 80–120 MXN for a filling meal.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Centro Histórico is best explored on foot. Keep an eye on belongings in crowded areas. The Metro is the most efficient and cheapest way to get around (5 MXN per ride).

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán neighborhood. Visit the iconic Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance as they sell out fast (entry ~270 MXN). Explore the colorful cobblestone streets around the museum and admire the colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, the charming heart of Coyoacán, free to explore. Browse the weekend artisan market (Bazar Artesanal de Coyoacán) for local crafts and souvenirs at reasonable prices. Visit the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán to experience authentic local market culture and taste regional snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood via Metro or Metrobús. Walk along tree-lined streets, admire Art Deco buildings, and soak up the bohemian atmosphere. Browse independent bookshops and quirky boutiques.

meals.breakfast: Café El Jarocho in Coyoacán — a legendary local coffee spot. Grab a café de olla and a pan dulce for under 50 MXN.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try enfrijoladas, tostadas de tinga, or fresh tlayudas for 60–100 MXN.
meals.dinner: Roma Norte street food scene — look for elote (corn) carts, quesadillas made fresh on the comal, and agua fresca stands. Full meal under 100 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets must be booked online well in advance — check the official website. Coyoacán is especially lively on weekends with markets and street performers.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early Metro ride to Chapultepec. Explore the massive Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — entry to the park is free. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Castle), which houses the National History Museum with panoramic views of the city (entry ~85 MXN). Enjoy the gardens and lakes inside the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) — one of the best museums in Latin America (entry ~85 MXN, free on Sundays). Spend a few hours exploring incredible pre-Hispanic artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Afterward, stroll through the Polanco neighborhood to window-shop and people-watch along Avenida Presidente Masaryk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Centro or Roma area. Visit a local pulquería (traditional pulque bar) for an authentic cultural experience — pulque is a traditional fermented agave drink very affordable at 30–50 MXN per glass. Enjoy the social atmosphere with locals.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast from a market stall near your hotel — huevos a la mexicana (scrambled eggs with tomato, onion, chili) with tortillas and coffee for 60–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Chapultepec Forest — buy fresh fruit, nuts, and snacks from park vendors for under 80 MXN, or eat at a nearby fonda (small local eatery) for a comida corrida at 70–100 MXN.
meals.dinner: Try a local taquería in Roma or Condesa — tacos de guisado (stewed filling tacos) are a budget staple at 15–20 MXN each. A full dinner with a drink costs around 100–150 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Anthropology is free every Sunday — if your schedule allows, shift this visit to Sunday for extra savings. Chapultepec is very popular on weekends so expect crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Xochimilco via Metro and light rail (total ~15 MXN). Rent a colorful trajinera (flat-bottomed boat) on the ancient Aztec canals — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Negotiate boat rental with a group to split costs (boats start around 300–500 MXN for 1–2 hours). Enjoy the festive atmosphere with floating food and music vendors on the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Xochimilco and visit the nearby Mercado de Jamaica, Mexico City's famous flower market — a stunning and free visual experience bursting with color and scent. Browse the stalls and interact with local vendors. Pick up affordable fresh flowers or unique items as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening stroll. Visit the rooftop terrace of a nearby building or café for views of the illuminated Zócalo. Do last-minute souvenir shopping at street markets. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area breakfast — a simple torta (Mexican sandwich) from a street vendor with café de olla for under 60 MXN.
meals.lunch: On the trajinera or at Xochimilco market — buy fresh quesadillas, tlayudas, or elotes from floating vendors for 30–60 MXN each.
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a local fonda or taquería in Centro — treat yourself to a slightly larger meal like mole enchiladas or chiles en nogada (seasonal) for 100–180 MXN as a farewell to Mexico City.

day_by_day.notes: Xochimilco is best visited on weekends when it's most lively, but weekdays are less crowded and boats may be cheaper to negotiate. Bargain politely for boat rentals. Keep small change handy for floating vendors. Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange transport to the airport in advance.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: Upon arrival after 22:30, freshen up and take a short walk near the hotel to get oriented. Grab a late-night snack from a nearby taqueria or convenience store if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night tacos from a street stand or 24-hour taqueria near the hotel — budget-friendly and authentically Mexican

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 22:30. Allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and transport to the hotel. Do not plan any sightseeing on Day 1. Rest is the priority to prepare for a full Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then head to the Historic Center (Centro Histórico). Visit the Zócalo — one of the largest city squares in the world — and explore the magnificent Metropolitan Cathedral. Walk through the ruins of Templo Mayor, the ancient Aztec temple unearthed in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's famous murals depicting Mexican history. Stroll through the surrounding streets of Centro Histórico, browsing artisan markets and colonial architecture. Visit the Mercado de Artesanías for local crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Condesa or Roma neighborhood for dinner and an evening stroll. Enjoy the tree-lined boulevards, Art Deco buildings, and vibrant café culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try chilaquiles or huevos rancheros, a classic Mexican morning staple
meals.lunch: Café de Tacuba in Centro Histórico — a historic mid-range restaurant serving traditional Mexican cuisine in a stunning colonial setting
meals.dinner: El Parnita in Colonia Roma — a beloved local spot known for creative Mexican street food and cocktails at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Centro Histórico is well-connected by Metro (Line 2, Zócalo station). Wear comfortable walking shoes. Keep an eye on your belongings in busy market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec. This is one of the greatest anthropology museums in the world, housing the famous Aztec Sun Stone and priceless pre-Columbian artifacts. Allocate at least 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bosque de Chapultepec — Mexico City's massive urban park. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) perched on a hill with panoramic views of the city. Explore the castle's museum dedicated to Mexican history and the Second Mexican Empire.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Polanco, Mexico City's upscale neighborhood, for an evening of window shopping along Presidente Masaryk Avenue and a mid-range dinner.

meals.breakfast: Panadería Rosetta in Roma Norte — a celebrated bakery famous for its guava-filled rolls and excellent coffee
meals.lunch: Food stalls inside Bosque de Chapultepec or a casual restaurant near the park entrance — try a torta or fresh fruit with chili and lime
meals.dinner: Contramar (book ahead) or a mid-range seafood/Mexican restaurant in Polanco — fresh fish tacos and ceviche are excellent choices

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is closed on Mondays. Chapultepec Park is free to enter; the castle and museum have a small admission fee (approx. $5–7 USD). Polanco is safe and walkable in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Columbian city located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive early to beat the crowds and the midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán, including the Temple of the Feathered Serpent (Quetzalcóatl) and the Palace of the Jaguars. Browse local vendors selling obsidian crafts and traditional souvenirs at the site exit. Return to Mexico City by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Unwind in the Coyoacán neighborhood — a bohemian, colonial-era district. Visit the colorful Jardín Centenario plaza and explore the local artisan market.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — aim to leave by 8:00 AM
meals.lunch: La Gruta Restaurant at Teotihuacán — a unique mid-range restaurant built inside a natural cave near the archaeological site, serving traditional Mexican dishes
meals.dinner: El Jarocho or a local cantina in Coyoacán — try enchiladas, mole, or pozole in this charming neighborhood known for its authentic food scene

day_by_day.notes: To reach Teotihuacán, take a bus from Terminal Central del Norte (about 1 hour, very affordable) or book a guided tour for convenience. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and bring water — the site is largely exposed. Teotihuacán admission is approx. $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul — The Blue House) in Coyoacán. This iconic museum is the former home of Frida Kahlo and showcases her life, art, and personal belongings. Book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mercado de Coyoacán for a vibrant local market experience — taste fresh tostadas, tlayudas, and tropical fruits. Walk to the nearby Museo León Trotsky, the former home of the exiled Russian revolutionary, for a fascinating historical detour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Enjoy a final dinner in a neighborhood close to the hotel to reminisce about the trip.

meals.breakfast: Café El Jarocho in Coyoacán — a legendary local coffee shop that has been serving Mexico City residents since 1953; pair with a fresh pastry
meals.lunch: Tostadas at Mercado de Coyoacán — try the famous tostadas de tinga or ceviche from the market stalls, an authentic and affordable mid-range experience
meals.dinner: Fonda El Refugio or a well-reviewed local restaurant near the hotel — enjoy a final taste of traditional Mexican cuisine such as chiles en nogada or mole negro

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets must be booked online well in advance — walk-in tickets are rarely available. Admission is approx. $12–15 USD. Coyoacán is best explored on foot. If departing the next morning, confirm your checkout time and arrange airport transport the night before.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Benito Juárez International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled towels, a signature cocktail, and a brief orientation of the resort's premium services. Settle into your suite and unwind.

meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the resort featuring Mexican comfort classics — warm tortilla soup, grilled quesadillas with Oaxacan cheese, and a selection of artisanal Mexican spirits to ease into your stay.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm early check-in or luggage storage if needed. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority after a late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Begin your first full day with a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort. Afterward, embark on a private guided tour of the Historic Center (Centro Histórico) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the magnificent Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), marvel at the Metropolitan Cathedral, and visit the ancient Templo Mayor ruins with an expert archaeologist guide who provides deep cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the iconic Palacio de Bellas Artes for a private docent-led tour of its stunning Art Nouveau architecture and world-class murals by Diego Rivera and David Alfaro Siqueiros. Afterward, stroll through the historic Alameda Central park before visiting the Franz Mayer Museum, one of Latin America's finest decorative arts collections, housed in a beautifully restored 16th-century hospital.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar in the Centro Histórico with panoramic views of the illuminated cathedral and Zócalo. Then proceed to dinner at Azul Histórico, a celebrated restaurant set in a colonial courtyard, known for elevating traditional Mexican regional cuisine with exceptional ingredients and presentation.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict with chorizo, avocado toast, and Mexican coffee or champagne.
meals.lunch: Curated tasting lunch at El Cardenal, a beloved Mexico City institution renowned for authentic Mexican cuisine — try the chiles en nogada or mole negro with handmade tortillas.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico — multi-course regional Mexican tasting menu with wine pairing, set in a stunning colonial courtyard. Expect dishes like duck in black mole, Veracruz-style sea bass, and traditional desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Templo Mayor private guide and Azul Histórico reservation well in advance. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for the Historic Center tour.

day_by_day.morning: Private chauffeured excursion to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán, approximately 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy a VIP sunrise experience with a private archaeologist guide. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and explore the Avenue of the Dead with exclusive insights into the Teotihuacán civilization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City and head to the upscale Polanco neighborhood — Mexico City's most glamorous district. Explore the world-class Museo Soumaya, home to over 66,000 works of art including pieces by Rodin, Dalí, and El Greco. Browse the luxury boutiques along Presidente Masaryk Avenue and the artisan galleries in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Experience one of Mexico City's most celebrated fine dining institutions — Pujol by Chef Enrique Olvera, consistently ranked among the world's top 50 restaurants. Enjoy the legendary tasting menu featuring the iconic Mole Madre, Mole Nuevo — a mole aged over 1,000 days — alongside innovative dishes rooted in Mexican culinary heritage.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh juices, pastries, yogurt parfait, and Mexican coffee.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort and enjoyed at Teotihuacán with views of the pyramids — artisanal sandwiches, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Pujol — world-renowned tasting menu with optional wine or mezcal pairing. Reserve months in advance. Dress code is smart casual to elegant.

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán visit requires an early 6:00–7:00 AM departure. Apply sunscreen and bring a hat — the pyramids offer little shade. Pujol reservation is essential and books out weeks to months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the bohemian and culturally rich neighborhoods of Roma and Condesa on a private food and culture walking tour. Visit local mercados, taste street food elevated to an art form — tlayudas, tamales, fresh-squeezed juices — and discover the Art Deco architecture, independent galleries, and lush tree-lined boulevards that define these iconic barrios.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) in Coyoacán — Frida Kahlo's iconic Blue House — with a private guide offering deep biographical and artistic context. Afterward, wander through the charming Coyoacán neighborhood, browse the artisan Mercado de Artesanías, and visit the tranquil Jardín Centenario plaza for a taste of authentic Mexico City neighborhood life.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private mezcal and tequila masterclass at a premium spirits lounge in Polanco or Roma, led by a certified sommelier. Learn the nuanced differences between artisanal mezcal producers and premium tequila expressions. Conclude the evening with dinner at Contramar, one of Mexico City's most beloved seafood restaurants, famous for its legendary tuna tostadas and whole grilled fish.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a charming Roma Norte café — Café Nin or similar — featuring avocado toast, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty single-origin Mexican coffee.
meals.lunch: Curated tasting lunch during the food tour in Roma/Condesa — multiple stops sampling marquesitas, local tacos, aguas frescas, and regional snacks.
meals.dinner: Contramar — iconic Mexico City seafood restaurant. Must-order: tuna tostadas, grilled fish with two salsas, and fresh ceviche. Pair with a crisp white wine or house margarita.

day_by_day.notes: Book La Casa Azul tickets and private guide in advance — entry is limited. The Roma/Condesa food tour is best done on foot; wear comfortable shoes. Contramar is very popular — reserve ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Begin your final morning with a luxurious spa treatment at the resort — a traditional Mexican Temazcal ceremony or a signature massage using local botanical ingredients. This ancient steam ritual offers both physical rejuvenation and deep cultural immersion, guided by a trained therapist versed in indigenous wellness traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) perched atop a hill in the vast Bosque de Chapultepec — one of the largest urban parks in the world. Explore the castle's opulent imperial rooms, sweeping city views, and outstanding collection of Mexican history murals. Afterward, browse the Museo Nacional de Antropología — arguably one of the greatest anthropology museums in the world — with a private guide to explore its extraordinary collection of pre-Columbian artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: For your farewell dinner, indulge in an exclusive chef's table experience at Quintonil, led by Chef Jorge Vallejo — another of Mexico City's globally acclaimed restaurants celebrated for its modern interpretation of Mexican ingredients and cuisine. Enjoy a personalized tasting menu with sommelier-curated wine pairings, followed by a nightcap at a sophisticated mezcal bar in Polanco before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the resort — full à la carte service with Mexican specialties such as chilaquiles verdes, huevos rancheros, fresh tropical fruit platters, and premium coffee or mimosas.
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Havre 77 or similar upscale bistro near Chapultepec — seasonal salads, refined Mexican-French fusion dishes, and a glass of Mexican wine.
meals.dinner: Quintonil — world-class tasting menu showcasing hyper-local, seasonal Mexican ingredients. Wine or mezcal pairing recommended. Smart elegant attire suggested for this farewell dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Schedule the Temazcal ceremony early in the morning for maximum relaxation benefit. Museo Nacional de Antropología is vast — a private guide ensures you see the highlights efficiently. Confirm checkout time and arrange private luxury transfer to the airport if departing the following day.
